data.one_liner: Dart bindings for the libsodium cryptographic library for Dart-VM and Web.
data.what_it_does: Provides an easy-to-use Dart API that mirrors the native libsodium C API, supporting secret-key cryptography, public-key signatures, hashing, random data generation, and more. Works on Android, iOS, Linux, Windows, macOS, and Web.
use_when: You need robust, high-performance cryptographic operations (encryption, hashing, digital signatures) in your Dart or Flutter app.
You need cross-platform cryptographic support for both native platforms and the web.
avoid_when: You only need simple base64 or basic hashing functions that are already covered by standard Dart libraries like `dart:convert` or `crypto` without native binary dependencies.
You want a purely pure-Dart implementation of cryptographic primitives without relying on native compilation or WASM/JS bundling.
strengths: Supports all major platforms including Dart-VM and Web.
Leverages native build hooks to build native dependencies on demand.
Provides SecureKey wrappers for managing sensitive material in memory securely.
weaknesses: Requires proper cleanup (disposing of `SecureKey` instances) to avoid memory leaks.
Web deployment requires manually downloading and adding the `sodium.js` script to your project via helper commands.
data.setup_notes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml. For web targets, you must run `dart run sodium:update_web` to download and integrate `sodium.js`. Native platforms build dependencies automatically using build hooks.
